title: Slow Down, Turn, Stop
bigQuestion: How can a rider slow down, turn and stop safely?

story.title: The Little Slope
story.kicker: The board speeds up on a slope. Jada learns how to slow it down.
paragraphs: Jada and her aunt go to the park. There is a long, smooth path with no cars. One part of the path tips down a tiny bit. It is a very gentle slope. Jada checks her helmet strap.
Jada rolls onto the slope. She did not push, but the board goes faster. The wind blows on her face. "Whoa!" she says. Her aunt walks fast beside her. "Drag your back foot," says her aunt.
Jada keeps her front foot on the board. She bends her front knee. She lowers her back foot. Her shoe brushes the ground. Shhh, shhh. The board slows down. Then it stops.
Jada laughs. "My shoe was like a brake!" Her aunt nods. "The ground rubs your shoe. That slows you." Jada walks back up. This time she slows down early, before she gets fast.
story.think: Why did the board go faster on the slope when Jada did not push?

lessons.title: Drag a Foot Gently
lessons.mainIdea: Brush your back foot lightly on the ground to slow down while your front foot stays on.
reading: First, roll slowly on flat ground. Turn your front foot so the toes point ahead. Bend your front knee. Keep most of your weight on that front foot.
Next, lower your back foot to the ground beside the board. Let the flat bottom of your shoe brush the ground. Press a little. The board slows down.
Press a little more to slow down more. Use the whole flat shoe, not just the heel. A heel alone can bounce. Never drag a foot hard all at once. This way of slowing is called a *foot brake*.

words.d: slowing down by brushing your back foot on the ground

look.title: Shhh, Shhh
look.text: Look at the boy rolling slowly on the blacktop. His front foot is on the board, toes pointing ahead. His front knee bends. His back foot comes down. The flat bottom of his shoe brushes the ground. Shhh, shhh. The board slows and stops.
look.prompt: Which foot stayed on the board? Which foot brushed the ground?

check.q: Which foot brushes the ground to slow down?
check.why: The back foot brushes the ground. The front foot stays on the board.

check.q: Which part of the shoe should touch the ground?
check.why: Use the whole flat shoe. A heel alone can bounce.

check.q: How do you slow down more?
choices: Press your foot a little more
check.why: Press a little more to slow down more. Do it gently, not all at once.

lessons.title: Rubbing Slows You
lessons.mainIdea: Friction is the rubbing that slows things down.
reading: Rub your hands together fast. Do they feel warm? Your hands rub and push on each other. That rubbing is called *friction*.
Friction slows moving things down. When your shoe brushes the ground, the ground rubs it. The rubbing slows your board. Your shoe works like a brake.
Rough ground makes more friction than smooth ground. Grass makes a lot. That is why a board stops fast on grass. Friction helps you stop.

words.d: the rubbing between two things that slows them down
something that slows down or stops a moving thing

look.title: How Hard You Press
look.cite: Example numbers to show the idea, not a real test
look.prompt: Which press stopped the board in the shortest space?

check.q: What is friction?
choices: A push that makes you fast
check.why: Friction is rubbing between two things. It slows them down.

check.q: Why does your shoe slow the board?
check.why: The ground rubs your shoe. That rubbing is friction, and it slows you.

check.q: Where does a board stop the fastest?
check.why: Grass makes a lot of friction. The board stops fast.

lessons.title: Lean on Your Toes
lessons.mainIdea: Press your toes down and the board turns toward your toe side.
reading: Stand on the board on grass first. Press down with your toes. The board tips toward your toes. The side your toes point to is the *toe side*.
Under the board are two metal parts called *trucks*. They hold the wheels. When the board tips, the trucks turn the wheels.
Now roll slowly on smooth ground. Press your toes a little. Bend your knees. Look where you want to go. The board curves to your toe side.

words.d: the side of the board your toes point to
the metal parts under the board that hold the wheels and help it turn

look.title: A Gentle Curve
look.text: Look at the girl rolling slowly. She bends her knees. She presses her toes down a little. The board tips toward her toes. She looks ahead, toward the bench. The board makes a gentle curve that way.
look.prompt: On grass, press your toes. Which way does the board tip?

check.q: You press your toes down. Which way does the board turn?
check.why: Pressing your toes tips the board toward your toe side. It turns that way.

check.q: What are trucks?
choices: Metal parts that hold the wheels
check.why: Trucks are the metal parts under the board. They hold the wheels and help it turn.

check.q: Where should you look when you turn?
check.why: Look where you want to go. Your body follows your eyes.

lessons.title: Lean on Your Heels
lessons.mainIdea: Press your heels down and the board turns toward your heel side.
reading: Your heels are at the back of your feet. The side of the board behind your heels is the *heel side*. Stand on the board on grass. Press your heels down.
The board tips toward your heels. Now try it while you roll slowly. Press your heels a little. Bend your knees. The board curves to your heel side.
Heel turns can feel strange. You cannot see behind you well. Turn your head and shoulders to look where you are going. Small leans make small turns.

words.d: the side of the board behind your heels
to tip your body a little to one side

look.title: Toes and Heels
look.text: Picture two riders on the playground. One presses her toes down. Her board curves toward her toes. The other presses his heels down. His board curves toward his heels. Both bend their knees. Both look where they want to go.
look.prompt: Which rider turned to the heel side? How do you know?

check.q: Where is the heel side of the board?
check.why: The heel side is the side of the board behind your heels.

check.q: You press your heels down. Which way does the board turn?
check.why: Pressing your heels tips the board toward your heel side.

check.q: How do you make a small turn?
choices: Lean as far as you can
check.why: Small leans make small turns. Start small.

lessons.title: Slopes Make You Faster
lessons.mainIdea: Gravity pulls you down a slope, so the board speeds up without a push.
reading: A ball on a slide rolls down. Nobody pushes it. A pull brings it down. That pull is called *gravity*. Gravity pulls everything toward the ground.
A *slope* is ground that tips down. On a slope, gravity pulls your board down. The board goes faster and faster. You do not need to push.
Learn on flat ground first. Later, a grown-up can find a tiny slope with no cars. Never ride down a street or a big hill. Practice slowing down before you try any slope.

words.d: the pull that brings things down toward the ground
ground that tips down, like a small hill

look.title: Rolling Down a Gentle Slope
look.cite: Example numbers to show the idea, not a real test
look.prompt: What happens to the speed as the board keeps rolling down?

check.q: What pulls a board down a slope?
check.why: Gravity pulls things down. On a slope, it pulls the board down and speeds it up.

check.q: What happens to a board on a slope?
check.why: Gravity pulls it down the slope, so it goes faster and faster.

check.q: Where should a new rider learn?
check.why: Learn on flat ground first. Practice slowing down before any slope.

lessons.title: Stop Before Too Fast
lessons.mainIdea: Start slowing down early, before the board gets too fast.
reading: Slow is easy to stop. Fast is hard to stop. So start your foot brake early. Do not wait until you are going fast.
Pick a stop spot before you roll, like a tree or a line. Start to slow down well before it. Then you can stop right there.
Feeling fast and scared? Bend your knees and get low. Brush your back foot gently. A grown-up can stand at your stop spot to help.

words.d: a place you choose ahead of time to stop the board

look.title: The Chalk Line
look.text: Look at the playground. A grown-up draws a chalk line. A girl rolls slowly toward it. Far from the line, she starts her foot brake. Shhh. She slows. She stops right at the chalk line. She smiles at her grown-up.
look.prompt: When did the girl start to slow down: near the line or far from it?

check.q: When should you start to slow down?
choices: Only after you pass your stop spot
check.why: Slow is easy to stop. Start your foot brake early.

check.q: What is a stop spot?
choices: A place you choose to stop
check.why: A stop spot is a place you pick ahead of time, like a line or a tree.

check.q: You feel fast and scared. What helps?
choices: Bend low and brush your back foot
check.why: Getting low helps you balance. A gentle foot brake slows you.

lessons.title: Step Off Safely
lessons.mainIdea: Slow down first, then step off with your back foot and walk it out.
reading: First, slow down until you roll like a walk. Next, step your back foot onto the ground. Then step your front foot off. Take a few walking steps.
Sometimes you tip. That is part of learning. Bend your knees and get low. Low falls are small falls. Try to roll onto your side.
Do not catch yourself with stiff, straight arms. That can hurt your wrists. Wrist guards and knee pads help. Get up slowly and check that you feel okay.

words.d: to get off the board by putting your feet on the ground
to get low and roll so a fall is soft

look.title: Getting Off
look.text: Step 1: Roll slowly, as slow as a walk. Step 2: Put your back foot on the ground. Step 3: Lift your front foot off the board. Step 4: Take a few steps. Step 5: Pick up your board so it does not roll away.
look.prompt: Act it out on carpet. Which foot steps off first?

check.q: What do you do before you step off?
check.why: Slow down first, until you roll like a walk. Then step off.

check.q: Which foot steps off first?
check.why: The back foot steps onto the ground first. Then the front foot.

check.q: You start to fall. What helps?
check.why: Low falls are small falls. Roll, and do not catch yourself with stiff arms.

review.q: What slows the board when your shoe brushes the ground?
review.why: The ground rubs your shoe. That rubbing is friction.

review.q: Which foot stays on the board in a foot brake?
review.why: The front foot stays on the board. The back foot brushes the ground.

review.q: You press your toes down. Where does the board go?
review.why: Pressing your toes turns the board to the toe side.

review.q: Why does a board speed up on a slope?
review.why: Gravity pulls the board down the slope. It goes faster.

review.q: Why should you start slowing down early?
review.why: Slow is easy to stop. Fast is hard to stop.
Bend low and roll. Low falls are small falls.
